breakdown.description: Inviscid flow assumptions are incompatible with the no-slip condition
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the incompatibility. It kept the term "inviscid fluid" from the original prompt but then immediately contradicted it by assigning a non-zero kinematic viscosity. This does not fix the core physical contradiction. The ground truth correctly resolves this by either changing the fluid to "viscous" or changing the boundary condition to "slip".

breakdown.description: No-slip condition requires viscosity to generate shear stress at the wall
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to fix this inconsistency. By stating the fluid is "inviscid" while also providing a viscosity value and keeping the no-slip condition, the agent has created a new, self-contradictory prompt rather than resolving the original error. The fundamental issue that a no-slip condition requires viscosity, which an inviscid fluid lacks, was not corrected.
